items.q: Excessive worry across many domains most days for 8 months with tension and insomnia best fits what?
items.exp: GAD requires months (DSM six) of difficult to control multi topic worry with somatic tension symptoms. Panic is episodic attacks; phobia is cued; adjustment follows stressor within shorter frame.
r: Incorrect. Panic attacks are discrete surges.
Correct. Chronic free floating worry is GAD.
Incorrect. Phobia needs specific cue.
Incorrect. Duration and breadth exceed adjustment pattern.
items.kp: Worrying about everything for months equals GAD.

items.q: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks plus persistent fear of more attacks and avoiding buses defines what?
items.exp: Panic disorder centres on unexpected attacks and anticipatory anxiety with avoidance that can generalise to agoraphobia. Interoceptive exposure and SSRIs form core treatment.
r: Incorrect. GAD worries without discrete unexpected attacks focus.
Correct. Panic disorder with avoidance.
Incorrect. Social fear is scrutiny based.
Incorrect. Obsessions drive compulsions, not panic avoidance.
items.kp: Fear of the next attack is the disorder.

items.q: Blood injury phobia uniquely requires which treatment adaptation and why?
items.exp: Diphasic vasovagal response drops blood pressure causing syncope, so tensing muscles during exposure maintains pressure. Other phobias use relaxation compatible exposure.
r: Incorrect. Relaxation worsens hypotensive faint.
Correct. Applied tension prevents fainting.
Incorrect. Beta blockers do not treat vasovagal phobia mechanism.
Incorrect. Exposure remains essential.
items.kp: Blood phobia: tense, do not relax.

items.q: First line drug class for panic disorder and GAD when medication is indicated is what?
items.exp: SSRIs (with CBT) are first line maintenance for panic and GAD, started low in panic sensitivity. Benzodiazepines suit brief crisis only due to dependence and exposure interference.
r: Incorrect. Long term benzodiazepines addict and block learning.
Correct. SSRIs first line.
Incorrect. Antipsychotics are not anxiety first line.
Incorrect. Tricyclics work but side effects demote them.
items.kp: SSRI plus therapy, not endless benzodiazepines.

items.q: New anxiety with weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance and lid lag needs which test first?
items.exp: Hyperthyroidism mimics anxiety with adrenergic systemic signs; TFTs are cheap and decisive. Imaging follows only with focal or refractory clues.
r: Incorrect. No focal neurology described.
Correct. Check thyroid function.
Incorrect. EEG suits episodic altered awareness.
Incorrect. Unrelated screening here.
items.kp: Anxious and thyrotoxic look alike: test TSH.

items.q: Episodic headache, palpitations, sweating and paroxysmal hypertension spells suggest which mimic?
items.exp: Catecholamine surges from phaeochromocytoma produce spell like anxiety with headache, sweating, palpitations and pressure spikes, confirmed by metanephrines. It is rare but classic and curable.
r: Incorrect. Hypothyroidism slows and cools.
Correct. Phaeochromocytoma spells.
Incorrect. Anaemia causes fatigue and pallor pattern.
Incorrect. Vitamin deficiency lacks spells.
items.kp: Anxiety in hypertensive spells: hunt catecholamines.

items.q: Graded exposure therapy works in phobia by which learning principle?
o: Extinction or inhibitory safety learning through non reinforced feared contact
items.exp: Repeated feared contact without catastrophe builds competing safety memory (inhibitory learning) reducing avoidance; escape during exposure undermines it, explaining benzodiazepine interference.
r: Incorrect. Punishment is not mechanism.
Correct. Safety learning through exposure.
Incorrect. Old fear memory persists but is inhibited.
Incorrect. Sedation can impede learning.

items.q: Teen avoiding presentations, blushing and fearing humiliation most likely has what?
items.exp: Social anxiety fears negative evaluation in social or performance situations from adolescence, impairing schooling. Treatment is CBT with social exposure plus SSRI when moderate severe.
r: Incorrect. No single object cue.
Correct. Social anxiety disorder.
Incorrect. Attacks are scrutiny cued, not unexpected.
Incorrect. Mutism is childhood speech pattern.
items.kp: Fear of being judged is social anxiety.

items.q: Why are benzodiazepines avoided as long term anxiety treatment?
o: Dependence, tolerance, falls, cognitive harm and blocking exposure learning
items.exp: Chronic use produces physiological dependence with withdrawal anxiety mimicking illness, impairs memory and balance, and prevents extinction learning in CBT, so guidelines limit to short crisis courses.
r: Incorrect. Sedation is their main acute effect.
Correct. Dependence and learning blockade.
Incorrect. Psychosis is not routine effect.
Incorrect. They remain legal controlled medicines.
items.kp: Short rescue only; chronic benzos trap anxiety.

items.q: Panic attack chest pain assessment principle is what?
o: Always attribute to panic in known patients
Exclude cardiac and pulmonary emergencies by risk assessment first presentations and atypical features
items.exp: Panic mimics ACS, PE and arrhythmia; first or atypical attacks need medical triage (history, ECG, troponin by protocol) before psychiatric attribution, even in anxious patients who also develop heart disease.
r: Incorrect. Known panic patients still infarct.
Correct. Rule out emergencies appropriately.
Incorrect. Sedation without triage is unsafe.
Incorrect. ECG is core chest pain triage.
items.kp: Panic is diagnosis after chest is cleared.
